title: Scaffold directory structure, SKILL.md, and test harness
description:

IMPORTANT: All files go in the REPO directory (hermes-da-kimi/), not ~/.hermes/. An install.sh script symlinks them into ~/.hermes/ for the hermes runtime. This way others can clone the repo and run install.sh.

- artist/{scripts,works,tests}
- plugins/artist/dashboard/dist/

- artist/PERSPECTIVE.md — template with 5 section headers from spec §3.5
- artist/studio.json — initial: {"schema_version":"1","setup_completed":false,"last_checked":null,"tools":{},"review_size":768,"model_family":"unknown"}

- install.sh — symlinks skills/artist, artist, and plugins/artist into ~/.hermes/

design: EC§3 (SKILL.md Before Code): write the contract first. EC§6 (Flat Modules): one dir per piece. EC§11 (Shared State Contracts): all JSON has schema_version='1'. EC§13 (Characterize Before You Change): the test harness lets subsequent tickets test against known-good fixtures. EC§19 (Edit-Test Cadence): every ticket includes its own tests from here on.

title: Tracer bullet: generate self-portrait, verify full script loop
description:
Validate the full stack by simulating a commission end-to-end — without requiring a live hermes-agent session.

This is the architecture proof. The agent (kbl/kimi) acts AS the artist: generates an image, writes the piece directory structure, runs every script against it, and verifies the loop works.

Steps:
1. Generate a self-portrait image using available tools. Try in order:
   - python3 + pillow: generate a 512x512 abstract image (shapes, gradients, noise)
   - ImageMagick: `magick -size 512x512 plasma:purple-blue output.png`
   - Fallback: create a 1x1 PNG with python3 (minimal but valid)

2. Create a piece directory following the spec:
   mkdir -p artist/works/<id>/thumbs
   Where <id> follows the format YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-MMMM-self-portrait

3. Write all required files in the piece directory:
   - output.png (the generated image)
   - statement.md (a brief artist statement about the self-portrait)
   - process.md (using the 5-section template from spec §6.2: Concept & Research, Approach, Code, Iterations, Final Notes)
   - meta.json (valid schema, all required fields, medium="image/png", tools_used=["pillow"] or whatever was used)
   - thumbs/thumb.jpg (300px wide resize of output)
   - thumbs/review.jpg (768x768 resize of output — default review size)

4. Copy output to artist/avatar.png (the agent's avatar).

5. Run validate-meta.sh on the piece's meta.json — must pass.

6. Run gallery.sh --json — must show the piece with total >= 1.

7. Run show.sh <id> --json — must return full piece data.

8. Run: echo "This is my first piece" | feedback.sh <id> --comment --json — must succeed.

9. Run: feedback.sh <id> --set-favorite true --json — must succeed. Verify meta.json updated.

10. Write a tracer-report.md at artist/tests/tracer-report.md documenting what worked and what failed.

This proves: piece creation → scripts read it → feedback mutates it → gallery lists it. The only thing NOT tested is hermes loading the SKILL.md and routing a commission — that's a manual test for the human patron later.
design: This is a tracer bullet per engineering_core.md 'Path to Prototype 1' (lines 386-407). Prove the full loop before building more. EC§13 (Characterize Before You Change): document actual behavior before expanding.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A piece directory exists at artist/works/<id>/ with valid ID format.
2. output.png is a valid image (file command confirms PNG).
3. avatar.png exists at artist/avatar.png.
4. meta.json passes: bash artist/scripts/validate-meta.sh artist/works/<id>/meta.json
5. statement.md and process.md are non-empty.
6. process.md has all 5 section headers (Concept, Approach, Code, Iterations, Final Notes).
7. thumbs/thumb.jpg and thumbs/review.jpg exist.
8. bash artist/scripts/gallery.sh --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['meta']['total']>=1"
9. bash artist/scripts/show.sh <id> --json | python3 -c "import sys,json; d=json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['success']"
10. Feedback round-trip: comment + favorite persist in meta.json after feedback.sh calls.
11. artist/tests/tracer-report.md exists.

title: Implement feedback.sh with tests
description:
Create ~/.hermes/artist/scripts/feedback.sh — adds patron feedback to a piece meta.json using atomic writes and idempotent verbs.

Flags: <id> (required positional), --set-favorite true|false, --set-discouraged true|false, --comment (reads text from stdin), --json.

IMPORTANT: Comment text is read from STDIN, never from shell arguments. This prevents shell injection.

Behavior:
1. Source helpers.sh. Validate piece ID with validate_id.
2. Validate comment text (from stdin): reject control chars (ASCII < 0x20 except \n and \t), max 2000 chars.
3. Read meta.json, apply feedback:
   - --set-favorite true: set patron_feedback.favorite=true, favorite_at=ISO8601 now.
   - --set-favorite false: set patron_feedback.favorite=false, favorite_at=null.
   - --set-discouraged true|false: same pattern.
   - --comment: read stdin, append {"text":"...","created_at":"ISO8601"} to patron_feedback.comments array.
4. Write meta.json back using write_atomic from helpers.sh.
5. Run validate-meta.sh on the result.
6. Return updated feedback state in envelope.

Write tests in ~/.hermes/artist/tests/test_feedback.sh:
- Test --set-favorite true sets flag + timestamp.
- Test --set-favorite false clears flag.
- Test --set-favorite true twice is idempotent (same result).
- Test --set-discouraged true sets flag + timestamp.
- Test --comment via stdin appends to comments array (run twice, verify 2 comments).
- Test comment with control char (printf '\x01bad') rejected.
- Test comment over 2000 chars rejected.
- Test newlines and tabs in comment are allowed.
- Test path traversal ID (../../etc/passwd) rejected.
- Verify original meta.json fields preserved after feedback mutation.
- Verify validate-meta.sh passes after each mutation.
design: EC§2 (One Envelope). EC§7 (Validate Edges): enum + regex at boundary. EC§9 (Append-Only): comments array grows, never shrinks. EC§16 (Input Hardening): reject control chars except \n and \t. EC§17 (Safety Rails): --set-discouraged is soft signal, not delete.
acceptance_criteria:
1. bash ~/.hermes/artist/tests/test_feedback.sh exits 0.
2. feedback.sh is executable.
3. --set-favorite true sets favorite=true with ISO8601 timestamp. Running it again is idempotent.
4. echo "text" | feedback.sh <id> --comment appends (append-only, never overwrites prior comments).
5. Control chars in comment rejected (except \n and \t). Path traversal in ID rejected.
6. Non-feedback fields in meta.json are preserved after mutation.
7. All writes use write_atomic (verify by checking for .tmp files during test — there should be none left).
8. validate-meta.sh passes after every mutation.

title: Vision step errors on every commission — 'analyzing page [error]' breaks self-review loop
description:
Every artist commission so far (Newborn, First Response, First Recognition) has hit '👁️ vision analyzing page  [error]' when the agent tries to load its own review.jpg into vision context. The agent's emergent workaround is to call Python pixel-statistics analysis (e.g. mean luminance) instead — which is creative but isn't what the spec promises. The whole 'review.sh returns review.jpg → agent loads it via vision → iterates' loop is currently broken. Architecture is sound; only the vision-input step fails.

Hypotheses to investigate: 
1. kimi-k2.6 hermes integration may not have vision wired through the terminal/file-load path. 
2. chafa preview may be confusing the model into thinking the terminal output IS the image. 
3. Image format/dimensions: reproduces both with 512x640 (aspect-preserved) and 512x512 (square). 
4. Hermes's vision tool may need a different invocation path than the agent is using.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Agent successfully loads its own review.jpg into vision context during a commission and produces a description of what it sees.
2. Self-review loop works without a Python-pixel-analysis fallback.
3. Either: fix is documented in SKILL.md (e.g. specific hermes vision invocation), or: hermes config/terminal toolset is updated to expose vision properly to kimi-k2.6.
notes:
Workaround in use: agent runs Python statistics on pixel values to evaluate brightness/composition. Surprisingly effective for catching too-dark renders (caught First Recognition v1 at avg luminance 28/255), but doesn't scale to higher-level critique (composition, color harmony, narrative reading).

Verified: error reproduces on kimi-k2.6 via Kimi Coding Plan provider, hermes 2026-05-03 main, with both 512x640 and 512x512 review.jpg sizes.
close_reason: Merged from overnight/hermes-da-kimi-6i6 via integrate/20261005 on 2026-10-21

title: SKILL.md: tighten 'before each commission' to fire on every commission, not just session start
description:
The artist SKILL.md context-loading section says 'At every session start, read these files: PERSPECTIVE.md, studio.json. Before each commission, also read: gallery.sh, patron feedback...' Kimi-k2.6 interpreted this as 'do it once per session' — it ran review.sh/show.sh/PERSPECTIVE.md/studio.json on the first commission of a fresh hermes session, then skipped all of those reads on the second commission of the same session.

Reproduction: 1) /reset hermes. 2) Commission a piece (X). 3) Without resetting, commission a companion (Y). The agent will have read all context on (X) but skipped it for (Y), relying on the in-session LLM context window for continuity rather than the on-disk gallery. This silently degrades the persistent-identity guarantee — the architecture's whole point is that pieces are anchored on disk, not in context.

Fix: rewrite the 'Context loading' section so the per-commission reads are explicitly required on EVERY commission regardless of session state. Suggested wording: 'Run review.sh and show.sh on relevant prior pieces at the start of every commission, even if you remember them from earlier in this session — your patron expects continuity that survives /reset.'
acceptance_criteria:
1. SKILL.md 'Context loading' section explicitly states per-commission reads happen on every commission, not just first.
2. Optionally adds a sentence explaining why (continuity must survive /reset).
3. After /reset + two consecutive commissions in one session, the second commission's tool log shows review.sh/show.sh/gallery.sh calls (manual verification, document in close reason).
4. No regression: validate-meta.sh + all existing tests pass.
notes:
Context: discovered during the post-overnight-kbl QA session on 2026-05-03. First commission ('Newborn') ran the full context-load chain. Second commission in same session ('First Response') skipped review.sh/show.sh entirely — went generate-id → python → done.
